decisions.evidence: Band s124-band1 line 2 and the full page line 2: a clear raised period sits at the far left end of the line, right after ידידיך. The page uses the same period after שְׁמֶךָ, יְמִינֶךָ, קְדֻשָּׁתֶךָ and תּוֹרָתֶךָ.

Band line 3: after וַעֲנֵנִי there are two stacked dots (a colon/sof-pasuq), followed by a wider space before יִהְיוּ. It matches the colon after וְגֹאֲלִי on line 4, not the single period used after the עשה למען clauses.

First word of the last small-type line (after וּכְשָׁנִים at the end of the line above), checked in the band and in jerusalem124.png. The letters run ק-ד-מ-נ-י-ו-ת. No vav-letter stands between מ and נ, and the holam is a dot over the mem (defective spelling). The only vav is the one in וֹת. The colon follows.

decisions.exact_text: לַ?יָ (patah under lamed and qamatz under the second yod are visible; a sheva under the first yod can be neither confirmed nor excluded)
decisions.evidence: jerusalem124.png, the word after וְעָרְבָה, is small type. Patah under ל and qamatz under the second yod show. The space under the first yod has at most a speck that is not clearly two vertical dots. Elsewhere on the page the larger-type יְיָ shows a sheva, but that cannot be used to fill this one.

The lower points of Jerusalem on 124 have already been sent to the human. They are not settled here. Observation only: in jerusalem124.png the vav after ר is a real shuruq-vav letter (וּ), and the dispute is limited to the vowel(s) under ל and מ.

Second occurrence, the last word of the page's prayer text (after the second וּכְשָׁנִים), in jerusalem124.png. Same letter sequence as the first: ק-ד-מ-נ-י-ו-ת with no vav-letter after מ, so holam-defective. The terminal mark is the heavier ׃ glyph, which counts as an ordinary colon.

remaining_uncertainties.evidence: At band resolution the counter of the first ת shows no distinct dot. This can't be confirmed either way; don't add the dagesh from memory without a higher-resolution check.
Band line 3 shows a short vertical stroke beside the hiriq under the shin, which looks like a meteg. It is small and close to the hiriq, so it's isolated as faint. Neither reading recorded one.
First word of small-type line 2. The bet's interior is too small and dark to show a dagesh clearly. Left unresolved; don't fill it.
See the decision above. Small type, and no clear two-dot sheva is visible.

notes: The packet's two קַדְמוֹנִיּוֹת entries share the same context string. They are the two separate occurrences, one at the start of the last small-type line and one at its end. Both are decided independently above.
